title: Integrated verifier-driven execution feedback and operator learning
question: Can post-execution verification improve sparse routing and can verified experience be converted into reusable, transferable transition operators?
hypothesis: Verifier-derived positives and execution-failing hard negatives should improve routing over outcome-only updates, while verified transitions should support predictive state transitions, structural abstraction, operator consolidation, durable reconstruction, and verified composition.

arms.name: outcome_only
arms.intervention: existing post-outcome pairwise successor router update

arms.name: verifier_feedback
arms.intervention: post-execution verifier positives and rejected hard negatives

endpoints.name: eval_top1_recall
endpoints.description: held-out target rank-1 recall after training

decision_rule.condition: Compare outcome_only and verifier_feedback on eval_top1_recall over the registered seeds; report admission, target rank and verification diagnostics for both arms.
decision_rule.licenses: a workload-specific test of execution-driven routing learning.
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal routing improvement or asymptotic sublinear scaling.

decision_rule.condition: A procedural mechanism is counted as supported only when its registered endpoint reaches its precommitted threshold on held-out or independently verified examples.
decision_rule.licenses: support for that mechanism on this synthetic workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal reasoning, broad-domain continual learning, or hardware speedup.

held_constant: factor-count/product-key geometry unchanged from current successor baseline
M=128 in the registered C5 execution-feedback measurement
training seed and evaluation seed separation
